components: Combine theatre theory, history and practice through performance visits, dramatic texts and a group performance concept, rehearsal and presentation.
A Cultural History of European Theatre: Antiquity to the Early Modern Period
The diagnostic language test and tutoring are additional required activities carrying no credits.
Introduction to Theatre Studies: Theories and Methods
Analyse acting, bodies, space, time and audience experience through weekly performance visits and academic writing.
Requires a positive first-year study recommendation in Theatre Studies and a pass in Dramaturgy. Dramaturgical research develops into a collaborative theatrical presentation.
Philosophy of Science: Arts and Cultural Studies
Blockbusters and Other Plays: Dutch Theatre History since 1638 in a European Context
Philosophy of Science in Theatre Studies
The study trip requires a positive first-year study recommendation in Theatre Studies. Preparation, visits, presentations and an individual study contribute to a reflective dossier.
Focus on Women: New Perspectives on Dutch Theatre History

Requires the first-year Theatre Studies certificate or another relevant first-year certificate. Earlier theatre-history study is recommended. Research uses the Allard Pierson theatre collection to investigate women’s overlooked contributions.

Six free-choice credits in year two and thirty-six in year three remain open. University electives, an approved minor, optional internship or approved study abroad may be used. Normally at most twelve credits may be introductory, or twenty-four under the specified approved-minor or same-language exceptions; external study needs Examination Board approval and compulsory courses cannot be duplicated.
Performing Ecocriticism: Theatre, Theory and Contemporary Climate Discourse
Requires a positive first-year study recommendation in the Humanities. Research examines ecocritical staging, representation, activism and climate discourse.
This six-credit restricted choice requires a positive first-year study recommendation. Study arts education in policy, schools and cultural institutions, including visits.

Free-choice space remains subject to the same level and approval rules. An internship is optional; the published twelve-credit example includes at least 336 hours and a report, agreed with the programme coordinator.

Requires the first-year Theatre Studies certificate and all compulsory second-year courses. Individually supervised research develops a question, analyses primary and secondary sources or data, and presents a critical argument with an identifiable original contribution.

candidateAssessment.concept: Theatre history, dramatic texts and dramaturgy
candidateAssessment.assessment: A whole24-course feasible trial combines all six literary courses, stylistic and rhetorical analysis, creative performance, film/adaptation, cultural history and research. Greek tragedy, drama as genre, myth/performance, cinematic acting/spectatorship and feminist interpretation are real substance. Together these do not sustain theatre-history progression, dramaturgical interpretation and live production analysis. Generalliterary or cinematic research is not automatically theatre-specific inquiry.

candidateAssessment.concept: Live performance, meaning and contemporary performance culture
candidateAssessment.assessment: A second full feasible24-course trial tests creative poetic performance, independent artistic practice, all six media courses, literary/adaptation methods, climatecommunication, rhetoricteaching and culturalhistory. Voice/embodiment, mise-en-scene, mediated spectatorship, documentaryproduction andenvironmentalaesthetics are genuine bridges. They form a creative/media programme without a sustained live-theatre analytical, dramaturgical andhistorical object. Absence of actortraining or a professional licence is not the criterion.

A third full feasible24-course trial tests culturalinstitutions/history, sociology/criticaltheory, qualitativeinterviews/archives, representation/race, publicrhetoric and actualschoolteaching. Museums, publicheritageprojects, materialcultureeducation andcommunity rhetoricaleducation provide concrete responses to society/education interests. Their combined object remains cultural/social inquiry rather than theatreinstitutions, theatreeducation andperformance research. This is not a claim that UCR lacks education, archives, spectatorship or performance altogether.

audience.programmeDescription: The University of Amsterdam’s Theatre Studies bachelor examines theatre and performance through history, theory, dramatic texts, live-performance analysis and dramaturgy. Research, performance visits and collaborative making connect these subjects; the programme also includes restricted choices, free study space and an individually supervised thesis.
audience.comparisonExplanation: UCR offers meaningful study of dramatic and literary texts, cinematic performance, poetic voice and embodiment, cultural history, representation and community teaching. These provide substantial related approaches. The strongest complete UCR programmes nevertheless centre literature, film and media, or broader cultural inquiry rather than sustained study of theatre history, dramaturgy and live-performance analysis. Their combined gaps in theatre’s defining subject matter and methods prevent a sufficiently close programme-level comparison.
